role: endocrinologist and PCP workflow scorer (D1, D5, D6, S)

scores.reason: Fasting-based HOMA-IR or OGTT-derived estimates only 'clarify metabolic dysfunction'; the project files record that no FIB-4, elastography or therapy step depends on it, so at most counselling.
sources: EASL-EASD-EASO 2024 PMIDs 38851997, 38852583, 38869512 full text (as recorded in project files, not re-read)

scores.reason: Primary care or hepatology can order a fasting insulin with glucose on a routine laboratory panel; one extra fasting draw, no specialist protocol. OGTT-derived variant adds steps. Measure type: fasting-based (HOMA-IR) and post-load.
Test burden 3 (one fasting venepuncture); false-result consequence 3 (no decision changes, so a wrong value causes at most extra counselling or retesting). Lower of the two is 3.
Without the measurement the usual FIB-4/elastography pathway and lifestyle therapy proceed unchanged, so marginal harm is minor.
sources: usecases-verified.md row 14 (no change to pathway or therapy depends on it)

scores.reason: C-peptide (fasting or MMTT-stimulated) supports classification as insulin-deficient and informs beta-cell reserve before TPIAT; the consensus diagnoses type 3c by glucose, HbA1c, OGTT and exocrine evidence, so C-peptide chooses among accepted options (insulin vs oral agents) rather than determining the diagnosis. Measure type: C-peptide.
Ordered by endocrinology or pancreas clinic (specialist outpatient); fasting C-peptide is simple but the stimulated MMTT adds a timed protocol; no cut-offs retrieved.

Test burden 3 (fasting) to 2 (MMTT, hypoglycaemia risk small); false-result consequence 2: preserved early C-peptide may delay insulin and misclassification as T2D (87.8% documented) leads to inappropriate oral agents, reversible with treatment. Lower is 2.

Default action without C-peptide is treating as T2D (documented misclassification); this causes delayed harm (poor control, late insulin) rather than immediate life threat. Alternative 3 if TPIAT candidacy decisions depend on it, which the files do not show.

JDS 2022 national expert criteria make fasting insulin >30 uU/mL the only biochemical major sign and set who gets genetic or antibody testing; per clarification 12 national diagnostic criteria elsewhere score 3. Not adopted by a US body; lipodystrophy guideline uses insulin requirement, not insulin level. Measure type: fasting-based.
sources: JDS working group 2022 PMID 35463863 full text via project files (PMC8980125)
Brown 2016 PMID 27710244 full text via project files

scores.reason: Specialist-only: endocrine or genetics clinics, with send-out antibody and genetic tests; the fasting insulin step is simple but the pathway is complex.

Test burden 3 (fasting draw); false-result consequence 3: a false negative (insulin below 30 in some genetic cases, or exogenous insulin) delays referral but the clinical clue (insulin requirement) remains; a false positive leads to extra antibody or genetic testing. Lower is 3, with exogenous insulin and assay under-reading at extreme values [recall] as caveats.
sources: usecases-verified.md row 12 (skeptic notes on JDS Tables 2 and 3)

scores.reason: Default is managing as common T2D; missed syndromic or type B IR carries serious morbidity (severe hyperglycaemia, organ injury, treatable immunosuppression or metreleptin missed).

Suppressed insulin and C-peptide at hypoglycaemia exclude hyperinsulinism and redirect to tumour imaging and IGF-II rather than insulinoma search; other tests (IGF-II, beta-hydroxybutyrate response) can partly substitute, hence 3 not 4. Insulin/C-peptide use for hypoglycaemia work-up, not an IR niche. Measure type: insulin and C-peptide (during hypoglycaemia).
sources: Hyperinsulinism guideline Table 2 (per project files, not re-read)

scores.reason: Endocrinology orders it in a hypoglycaemia work-up, often a supervised fast or sample at spontaneous hypoglycaemia, which is a timed protocol; specialist.

Test burden 2 (needs hypoglycaemic sample, supervised fast carries hypoglycaemia risk); false-result consequence 2 (misclassifying as insulinoma leads to futile imaging or surgery, reversible). Lower is 2.
Default without the result is an insulinoma search; harm is delay in finding the causative tumour with recurrent hypoglycaemia (serious morbidity).

Kidney clearance falsely raises C-peptide, so the result is a caution on interpretation of rows 6-11 (counselling or caveat); no decision is set by it and no CKD correction is validated. Measure type: C-peptide, glucose/C-peptide ratio, UCPCR.
sources: Jones and Hattersley 2013 PMID 23413806 full text via project files

scores.reason: Specialist-only with no standard protocol; UCPCR is not routine and correction methods are poorly validated.

Test burden 3 (blood or urine sample); false-result consequence 2: falsely reassuring C-peptide in CKD may delay insulin or hide secretagogue hypoglycaemia risk, harm reversible with treatment. Lower is 2.
Default is classifying from an uncorrected C-peptide; misread can delay insulin or leave sulfonylurea hypoglycaemia risk in CKD, moderate delayed harm.

Scored for part (b), first-trimester HOMA-IR to predict GDM: no established action follows; the OGTT at 24 to 28 weeks decides. Part (a) GCK testing is glucose-based and not an insulin use. Measure type: fasting-based HOMA-IR.
sources: ANZ 2025 PMID 40640995 full text (per project files)

scores.reason: Obstetrics or midwifery owns GDM screening and a first-trimester fasting draw is possible, but no defined test pathway exists; scored low for the unvalidated use.
Test burden 3 (one fasting draw); false-result consequence 3 (anxiety or earlier glucose testing; no treatment change). Lower is 3.
Default is standard OGTT-based GDM screening, so omitting HOMA-IR causes little marginal harm; alternative 2 only if early prediction led to earlier treatment, which is untested.

Low urinary or serum (fasting and post-glucagon or meal) C-peptide is criterion 3 of three in the Japan Diabetes Society fulminant T1D criteria, so it determines the diagnosis under national criteria (clarification 12: 3). Not adopted in the US; treatment (insulin, DKA care) is the same either way. Measure type: C-peptide.
sources: Imagawa et al. 2012 PMID 24843620 PMC4015434 full text (per project files)

scores.reason: Ordered by the admitting team or endocrinology after DKA; serum C-peptide is simple, the 24-hour urinary option and stimulated test add steps; no US pathway.

Test burden 3 (blood or urine sample; glucagon stimulation is optional); false-result consequence 3 (insulin therapy is given regardless; a wrong label affects follow-up and counselling only). Lower is 3.
Default is insulin and DKA treatment, which is correct for fulminant T1D, so marginal harm from not measuring is limited to missed recognition of the subtype (follow-up, associated conditions).

anchor_issues: Row 12 D1: JDS criteria are national (Japan) diagnostic criteria; clarification 12 gives 3, but they are not adopted in the US and the lipodystrophy guideline names no insulin threshold. Chose 3, low confidence.
Row 35 D1/D5/D6/S: the row combines (a) GCK trigger (glucose-based) and (b) HOMA-IR; scored only (b) as the insulin use.
Row 21 setting: hypoglycaemia work-up is not an IR use; D1 scored for the insulin/C-peptide exclusion step.
Row 46 D1: national (Japan) criterion scored 3 per clarification 12, although no US body adopted it.
assumptions: Scored from project files only; no new searches run, so no new evidence was added. Guideline read levels are those recorded in usecases-verified.md, not re-read.
Setting for row 46 assigned as inpatient or procedural because fulminant T1D presents with ketoacidosis at admission.
